finding.claim: /settings/password sets the password to the hardcoded literal 'hunter2' for any logged-in session, with no current-password check or re-authentication, and no CSRF protection in the handler. Hardcoded credential in source.
finding.source: Any request carrying a valid logged-in session cookie for the victim. Attacker's own session needs no escalation; cross-site POST (CSRF) is a precondition to verify via SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, which is not set in this file.

trace.note: login_required aborts 401 when uid absent from session
set_password(g.uid, 'hunter2'); request body never read, literal password written

finding.guards_checked: login_required blocks anonymous callers (only control on path). No current-password verification, no re-authentication, no CSRF token in handler. SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE config not visible in this file. Set_password is a stub here, so the write is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: login_required (routes.py:8-16) aborts 401 when "uid" is not in the session, and it is the only control on the path. No current-password check, re-authentication, or CSRF token exists in the handler (routes.py:41-45). SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE is not set in this file, and the Flask app config is not visible.
verdict.reason: The trace matches routes.py:41-45: login_required (routes.py:11-12) blocks anonymous callers and set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") at routes.py:44 is reached only with a session uid. The attacker can therefore only set the password of the account behind their own session, which gains them nothing. Harm to a victim needs a cross-site POST from the victim's browser, and whether that cookie is sent depends on SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, which is configured outside this file. Also, set_password at routes.py:52-53 is a no-op stub, so the write itself is unverified.
